body.statement: When \(C_x\) has zeros or the anchor-zero subspace \(D_{a_s}\) is not contained in the range of \(\mathscr L_{s,x,u,w}\), characterize exactly which target directions admit two-sided observationally equivalent causal perturbations and determine whether point identification is equivalent to annihilation of the feasible two-sided tangent cone produced by the support-face route.
body.justification: Zeros in the common proxy kernel or an outcome support with deficient one-way tangent rank are the boundaries at which the division or two-sided support argument fails, so the tangent-rich theorem does not settle every sparse-proxy case.
body.gap: Neither the nonunique-bridge literature nor existing proxy bounds characterize the causal tangent cone of a fixed observed-law support face.
body.consumer: The answer would determine which exact-nullity conclusions survive sparse assay categories and structural zero outcomes instead of requiring artificial smoothing.
